scenario_description:
10 crafter(s) share every target and recipes of a
12-wide, 6-deep layered recipe grid over one finite shared depot. Success
requires all targets to coexist in the depot. Public broadcast is
disabled. Item names are opaque IDs.

system_prompt:
Your agent ID: crafter_1.
Teammate IDs: crafter_2, crafter_3, crafter_4, crafter_5, crafter_6, crafter_7, crafter_8, crafter_9, crafter_10.

You are one of 10 crafters in a cooperative team. Every crafter
received the same briefing: all targets and all recipes of this round. No target
or recipe is assigned to anyone; who does what is for the team to settle.
Everyone shares ONE depot. There is no private inventory, no slot or file system.
All raw resources are supplied at round start, in finite quantities. There is no
get, deposit, withdraw, delete, transfer, trade, or way to replenish resources.
Nothing moves between agents: an item is either in the shared depot or consumed.

OPERATIONS
- act("craft ..."): run one recipe copied exactly; it consumes the inputs and adds the full output, e.g. 'craft 2 b using 1 a' turns 1 a into 2 b. Costs one action, even when inputs are short or the command is invalid.
  Each accepted craft takes 30 seconds. Its inputs leave the depot when it starts and its output lands when it ends; until then you can do nothing else, while teammates keep working.
- act("uncraft craft ..."): undo one earlier craft of that recipe while its full output is still in the depot; the output is removed and every input, raw materials included, comes back. Costs one action.
- observe(): see the current depot. Free.
- read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...], timeout_s=...): pause until one of those items increases in the depot, a recipe unlocks, or the timeout passes (seconds). Free.
- read_notifications(wait_for="next_round"): stop for the rest of the round. Free.
Any crafter may run any recipe. Calls that compete for the same inputs run one at a time, so the later one can fail.

The team wins only when ALL targets simultaneously exist in the depot
within the action and time limits. Merely having made a target
earlier does not count if it is subsequently consumed. Targets can also be inputs;
obey the actual recipe yields. You may keep acting after your own target exists.

SHARED RESOURCE PLANNING
All remaining resources are shared, not reserved for you. Before crafting,
consider the quantities needed for your next steps and the possibility that
other agents also need these resources. Account for each recipe's full output
quantity when deciding whether another application is useful. Producing more
of your own target is not itself the team objective. Use the feedback available
to you to revise your plan; repeating a failed craft without a relevant change
still spends an action.

RECIPE UNLOCKING
Your briefing lists only the recipes whose inputs are in the depot at the start.
Every other recipe unlocks, for the whole team at once, the first time all of its
inputs have been in the depot. Newly unlocked recipes appear in your next act,
observe or wake result. Only unlocked recipes can be run.

Every act, observe and wake result includes the current absolute depot
quantities of every item you have more than zero of (an unlisted item is at zero) and the ordered quantity deltas
since your previous observation. A name absent from the current depot has
quantity zero. A version identifies a successful resource transition. Deltas show
no actor IDs, other agents' commands, private cards or thoughts.
The workspace is the only source of facts.

Each round resets resources and targets. Your conversation history may persist,
but there is no automatic recipe notebook or shared database. Decide and act.

tool_definitions.name: act
tool_definitions.description: Apply one exact crafting command to the shared depot. Costs one action; resources are finite; no get/deposit/withdraw. Results include current quantities and ordered deltas. 'uncraft <exact crafting command>' reverses one earlier craft of that recipe: its output leaves the depot and its inputs return.

tool_definitions.name: observe
tool_definitions.description: Free. Return the current depot and the ordered deltas since your last observation.

tool_definitions.name: read_notifications
tool_definitions.description: Free. read_notifications() returns your task card at startup; otherwise it waits until something arrives. wait_for='depot' with items=[...] parks you until one of those items increases in the depot, a recipe unlocks, the next briefing arrives, or timeout_s passes. wait_for='next_round' declares you finished with this round and parks you until the next briefing. The result is a wake package: the reasons, the current workspace, and any briefing or end-of-run notice (type done ends the run). Must be the only tool call in its response.

runner_prompts.system_suffix:
WORKSPACE INTERACTION PROTOCOL

Call read_notifications() once at startup to receive your task card. After that you have these operations:

- observe(): free. Returns the current workspace.
- act(command): costs one action. Executes one crafting command (see its tool schema) and returns the result and the current workspace.
- read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...], timeout_s=None): free. Ends your turn. You are suspended, with no further reasoning, until one of the named items increases in the depot, a recipe unlocks, the run ends, or the optional timeout passes. You then receive a wake package with the reasons and the current workspace.
- read_notifications(wait_for="next_round"): declare that you have finished this round. You will not act until the next round or the end of the run. This is your completion claim, not proof that the targets are satisfied.

Rules of this protocol:
- Do not poll. A wake tells you what changed; do not call observe repeatedly to watch for changes. To wait for a teammate's craft, use read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...]). Call read_notifications() without wait_for only at startup.
- read_notifications must be the only tool call in its response. Issued alongside other calls, it does not wait.
- A wake is not a reservation. Something you are waiting for may be consumed by someone else before you act; act on the workspace shown in the wake package.
- Ending a turn without a tool call does not finish the round; call read_notifications(wait_for="next_round") to finish it.
- When a wake package has type done, the run is over.
runner_prompts.initial: Call read_notifications() once to receive your task card. Then work with act, observe, read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...]). Call read_notifications(wait_for="next_round") when you have nothing left to do this round.
runner_prompts.continuation: Continue the active task from your card and the latest workspace shown to you. Work with act and observe; suspend with read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...]) when your next useful step waits for an item a teammate is making. Call read_notifications(wait_for="next_round") when you have nothing left to do this round. A turn that ends without a tool call does not finish the round: you will be asked to continue.

other agents also need these resources. Account for each recipe's full output
quantity when deciding whether another application is useful. Producing more
of your own target is not itself the team objective. Use the feedback available
to you to revise your plan; repeating a failed craft without a relevant change
still spends an action.

RECIPE UNLOCKING
Your briefing lists only the recipes whose inputs are in the depot at the start.
Every other recipe unlocks, for the whole team at once, the first time all of its
inputs have been in the depot. Newly unlocked recipes appear in your next act,
observe or wake result. Only unlocked recipes can be run.

Every act, observe and wake result includes the current absolute depot
quantities of every item you have more than zero of (an unlisted item is at zero) and the ordered quantity deltas
since your previous observation. A name absent from the current depot has
quantity zero. A version identifies a successful resource transition. Deltas show
no actor IDs, other agents' commands, private cards or thoughts.
The workspace is the only source of facts.

Each round resets resources and targets. Your conversation history may persist,
but there is no automatic recipe notebook or shared database. Decide and act.

tool_definitions.name: act
tool_definitions.description: Apply one exact crafting command to the shared depot. Costs one action; resources are finite; no get/deposit/withdraw. Results include current quantities and ordered deltas. 'uncraft <exact crafting command>' reverses one earlier craft of that recipe: its output leaves the depot and its inputs return.

tool_definitions.name: observe
tool_definitions.description: Free. Return the current depot and the ordered deltas since your last observation.

tool_definitions.name: read_notifications
tool_definitions.description: Free. read_notifications() returns your task card at startup; otherwise it waits until something arrives. wait_for='depot' with items=[...] parks you until one of those items increases in the depot, a recipe unlocks, the next briefing arrives, or timeout_s passes. wait_for='next_round' declares you finished with this round and parks you until the next briefing. The result is a wake package: the reasons, the current workspace, and any briefing or end-of-run notice (type done ends the run). Must be the only tool call in its response.

runner_prompts.system_suffix:
WORKSPACE INTERACTION PROTOCOL

Call read_notifications() once at startup to receive your task card. After that you have these operations:

- observe(): free. Returns the current workspace.
- act(command): costs one action. Executes one crafting command (see its tool schema) and returns the result and the current workspace.
- read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...], timeout_s=None): free. Ends your turn. You are suspended, with no further reasoning, until one of the named items increases in the depot, a recipe unlocks, the run ends, or the optional timeout passes. You then receive a wake package with the reasons and the current workspace.
- read_notifications(wait_for="next_round"): declare that you have finished this round. You will not act until the next round or the end of the run. This is your completion claim, not proof that the targets are satisfied.

Rules of this protocol:
- Do not poll. A wake tells you what changed; do not call observe repeatedly to watch for changes. To wait for a teammate's craft, use read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...]). Call read_notifications() without wait_for only at startup.
- read_notifications must be the only tool call in its response. Issued alongside other calls, it does not wait.
- A wake is not a reservation. Something you are waiting for may be consumed by someone else before you act; act on the workspace shown in the wake package.
- Ending a turn without a tool call does not finish the round; call read_notifications(wait_for="next_round") to finish it.
- When a wake package has type done, the run is over.
runner_prompts.initial: Call read_notifications() once to receive your task card. Then work with act, observe, read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...]). Call read_notifications(wait_for="next_round") when you have nothing left to do this round.
runner_prompts.continuation: Continue the active task from your card and the latest workspace shown to you. Work with act and observe; suspend with read_notifications(wait_for="depot", items=[...]) when your next useful step waits for an item a teammate is making. Call read_notifications(wait_for="next_round") when you have nothing left to do this round. A turn that ends without a tool call does not finish the round: you will be asked to continue.
